Fresh powder in April and near-whiteout conditions made for a wild, rewarding day on the mountain; Colleen skied untracked snow while snowfall reduced visibility to the treeline by early afternoon.

**Highlights:**
- [Kirkwood Mountain Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkwood_Mountain_Resort) — situated at roughly 7,800 feet base elevation in the Sierra Nevada, Kirkwood receives one of the highest average annual snowfalls of any California resort, exceeding 350 inches, making a powder day this late in the season less shocking than it sounds.

A midday summit selfie at Kirkwood captured the resort village below and a pink-clad skier carving the slope behind — clear skies, cumulus clouds, classic Sierra spring conditions.

**Highlights:**
- [Kirkwood Mountain Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkwood_Mountain_Resort) — situated at 7,800 feet base elevation in Alpine County, Kirkwood receives among the highest average snowfall of any Lake Tahoe–area resort, often exceeding 500 inches annually, due to its position directly in line with Pacific storm tracks.
